description:
JMAP-sc1b is a review-shaped epic (type=epic, label=review) that appears in the /do-beads ready frontier despite Mark's 2026-05-12T02:49Z note: 'the autonomous /do-beads loop should not be picking this up as actionable — it filters epics from ready anyway. Removing human to clean the human-label list.'

The literal /do-beads rule (file: ~/.config/opencode/commands/do-beads.md, last updated 2026-05-10) says delegate review-shaped epics to bd-review-loop. But:

1. Mark's mental model was that /do-beads filters epics from ready. The rule does NOT filter epics — it only filters human-labeled beads.

2. The prior bd-review-loop run at 2026-05-11T17:08Z hit a permission ask (RUSTDOCFLAGS cargo doc --workspace --no-deps) and stalled, because the spawned opencode subprocess was not invoked with --dangerously-skip-permissions. Re-running risks the same deadlock from inside a /do-beads session.

3. All P0/P1/P2 children of JMAP-sc1b from the prior 3 bd-review-loop runs are already closed; only 4 P2/P3 cleanup beads remain (.17, .109, .110, .111). Re-triggering the review loop now would either re-find the same residual P3s or, more likely, find nothing new.

Resolution options:
(a) Update /do-beads rule to also filter type=epic from the ready frontier, leaving review epics for explicit operator action.
(b) Re-add the 'human' label to JMAP-sc1b indefinitely until the next manually-triggered review pass.
(c) Accept the literal rule — autonomous /do-beads sessions will run bd-review-loop on every ready review epic, with the deadlock risk above as the cost.
(d) Update the rule to delegate ONLY when no recent run-bd-review-loop-* labels exist within the last N hours (suggests this epic is already mid-cycle).

This session followed option (a)-equivalent behavior: skip JMAP-sc1b, work the next ready bead, file this meta-bead for the policy decision.
title: Policy: should /do-beads delegate review-shaped epics or skip them?
